workflow: Multiple threads request a lazily generated encoded representation of the same shared value while its cached representation is absent.
Each thread observes the missing cache and independently generates and publishes the representation without synchronization.
The representation pointer and its associated length are updated concurrently, allowing unsynchronized reads and writes or inconsistent publication.
A caller observes the concurrently modified cache, producing a data race instead of safely reusing one fully initialized representation.
summary: Concurrent lazy-cache initialization races during shared representation publication
decision_reason: No existing cluster captures an unsynchronized lazy initialization of shared cached representation data; the nearby concurrency clusters involve different mechanisms such as resource-handle mutation, identifier collisions, or ownership-retention transitions.
